title: Control: actions, the mover, the navigator and the client
tagline: Decisions turned into key plans; routes carried out closed loop; keys mailed to the player
summary: Everything the stack decides ends up here as a key plan: a list of timed key events for the elevated key player, handed over as files in lab/inbox and answered in lab/outbox (client). Actions turns one action at a time (a throw, a walk, a pick-up, a potion) into such a plan; the Mover carries out one route move closed loop; the Navigator gets her onto a platform by chaining many moves into one plan, watching it 15 times a second and cutting, splicing or queuing plans as she goes. Keymap and timeline supply her keys and MapleHelper's own combo timelines.
details_md:
Nothing in this slice presses a key itself. MapleStory runs as administrator and Windows blocks input from normal
programs into it, so one small elevated process, the **key player** (`control/player.py`, another slice), presses the
keys. Everything here talks to it only through files: `client.send` writes a **plan** as JSON into `lab/inbox/`, the
player renames it to `.running` when it takes it, plays it, and writes the result into `lab/outbox/`.

A plan is a list of timed events, `[ms into the plan, key name, "down" | "up"]`, key names as `config.toml` names them
(mouse plans use `[ms, "mouse", x, y]`). A plan may also say how long it lasts (`end_ms`) so the next plan starts the
moment it ends, and a running plan can be cut short (a `.cancel` file) or taken over mid-play by another (a `.splice`
file), the arrow held kept held.

Three layers of "doing" sit on the client:

- **Actions** (`actions.py`): one key plan per action of hers (a throw, a jump throw, a jump back, a walk with pick-up
  pressed all the way, pick-ups standing, a potion, pet food), each blocking until the player has played it. It also
  keeps the timing every plan must respect: her **attack lock** (730 ms after an attack key the game ignores jumps and
  attacks) and the **arrow lock** (an arrow pressed too soon after an attack key, 0.59-0.62 s as measured, only moves her
  from about 0.79 s after the key, so no plan's first arrow goes down before 0.8 s), and which way she faces, by her keys and by the frame, which decides whether a throw taps the arrow to turn her first.
- **The Mover** (`mover.py`): one route move (`motion.route.Move`) at a time, closed loop: a look, one key plan from
  wherever she stands, a look once she has settled. It is the fallback for moves the chain planner can't predict
  (climbing down a rope, which needs her lined up on its top; jumping off a rope sideways; run-ups she has to back off
  for), and gets her off ropes.
- **The Navigator** (`navigator.py`, 4,437 lines): gets her onto a platform. Each **pass** looks, plans a route
  (`motion.route.Planner`, Dijkstra over every move the physics allows), and chains as many of its moves as it can
  predict into one continuous key plan (`motion.flow.Flow.chain`: a **chain** of **legs**, one leg per move; a chain is
  cut off for length after 5 legs or 3.5 s, `flow.MAX_LEGS` and `MAX_SECONDS`, and the next follows on). While a chain plays it
  **glances** at her minimap dot and HP at perception's 15 states a second: a touch or being off the planned path cuts
  the plan; a monster coming into a leg still to come has the chain **replanned** and spliced in where she'll be 40 ms
  on; late in a chain the next one is planned from a look and **queued**, so she runs on without stopping.

Monsters are why the navigator is so large. Without an **escort** (mode `avoid`), each chain keeps clear of every
monster: her body's box against each monster's wherever it can walk by then. A blocked move costs extra so a way around
wins, else she waits a few looks, else the **evade step** takes her to a refuge, else she goes past. With an escort
(modes `hunt` and `transit`: the hunter's fights on the way, `behavior.fight.FightOnTheWay`, plugged in through the
`Escort` protocol) she shoots what's in her
way and keeps clear only of the kinds whose touch counts. Special handling covers her invulnerability after a touch
(1.45 s, during which her chains may pass a monster), the top of a rope (hanging under it until the way up clears) and
where a knock lands her.

Two smaller modules deal with keys themselves: **keymap** follows her keys to wherever the game's KEY BINDINGS window
shows their functions and remembers that per character; **timeline** runs MapleHelper's own combo code on a virtual
clock, so tests and the `combo` and `do` commands play exactly what the helper plays, and loads her setup from
`config.toml`.

By the layer rules (`tests/test_architecture.py`) control may import perception, localization and motion (plus the
shared modules); behavior sits above it and drives it: the hunter owns her `Actions` and makes navigators
(`Hunter.navigator`, with the fights on the way as escort or without), the tour and the hunt loop call `Navigator.go` /
`begin` + `step`, and the Lie Detector retreat builds its own navigator on `Actions.moves_only()`.

modules.details_md:
The package docstring describes control as "decisions turned into key plans for the elevated key player, and the
closed loops that carry out moves and routes", plus the player itself and the Lie Detector alarm. It lists the modules
one line each and states the rule `tests/test_architecture.py` enforces: control may import perception, localization,
motion and the shared modules.

It also records one constraint that shapes the whole package: the player (`player.py`) runs as administrator and loads
its code once, so what it imports must stay small. `tests/test_architecture.py` checks it (`test_the_elevated_player_loads_only_what_it_needs`):
loading the player must bring in nothing of behavior, motion, localization, attack, ui, the simulator, the game data or
gamelab's C pieces. So `player.py` (another slice) imports only `paths`, `window`, `control.alarm` and the Lie Detector's
spotter, while `client.py`, `actions.py`, `mover.py` and `navigator.py`, which run in the ordinary (unelevated)
command processes, import freely from the layers below.

The file defines no names; there are no key items.

modules.title: Navigator
modules.tagline: Gets her to a platform: plans, chains moves into one plan, watches, replans.
modules.summary: The biggest file in the stack (4,437 lines). A trip (`go`, or `begin` then `step`) is a loop of passes: look, plan a route (motion.route.Planner), chain as many predictable moves as possible into one key plan (motion.flow.Flow.chain), deal with any monster in the way (shoot, go around, hop, wait, evade, or pass), send the chain and watch it about 15 times a second, cutting it, splicing in a replan, or queuing the next chain as she goes. Moves the chain can't predict go to the Mover.
modules.details_md:
**How the file is laid out.** Most of its length is tunables with the measurements behind them, and a few large
procedures. Line ranges:

| Lines | Part | What's there |
|---|---|---|
| 1-41 | docstring | look -> plan -> chain -> one key plan -> check where she landed |
| 78-775 | tunables | 167 module-level constants (tunables, feature flags, the mode names), most with the incident or A/B numbers behind them |
| 778-1041 | types | `Escort` (what the fights on the way provide), `TopPrice`, `_Wait`, `Trip`, `KeyNames`, `_Running`, `_Ahead`, `Choice`, `TripState` |
| 1043-1218 | trip API | `__init__`, `go`, `begin`, `step`, `leaves_at`, `fresh` |
| 1220-1337 | `_pass` | one pass: the decision procedure |
| 1341-1487 | the route | `_look`, `_plan`, `_route` (a way chosen and kept), `_way_through` (the loot chain), `_penalty`, `_made` |
| 1488-1716 | monsters for a plan | `_chain_monsters`, `trip_monsters`, `remembered`, `hidden_tracks`, `_walking`, `_toucher`, `_ghost` |
| 1717-2147 | meeting monsters | `_chain`, `_pricing`, `_clear_landing`, `_meet`, `_shoot_ahead`, `_last_shot`, `_regardless`, `_wait_for_monster`, `_worth_waiting` |
| 2148-2475 | the evade step | `_evade_step`, `_refuge`, `_contact`, `_go_past`, `_within_window`, `_around` |
| 2476-2877 | carrying out | `_carry_out_chain`, `_carry_out_move`, `_move_watch`, `_arrival_clear`, `_onto_platform`, `_rope_top`, `_immunity`, `_after_chain`, `_note_landing` |
| 2878-3164 | the watch | `follow`, `_watch`, `_watching` (the glance loop), `_landing_calls` |
| 3165-3500 | replanning | `_switch`, `_take_over`, `_splice_point`, `_stop_calls`, `_knock_landing`, `_keys_seen`, `_queued_meets` |
| 3501-3981 | ropes | `_climb_on`, `_hang_check`, `_hang`, `_hang_judge`, `_walks_off`, `_take_now`, `_knock_cost` |
| 3982-4255 | glance helpers, follow-ons | `_coming`, `_room_to_stop`, `_track_of`, `_placed`, `recover`, `_tail`, `_look_ahead`, `_queue_next` |
| 4257-4437 | module helpers | `rope_at_top`, `standing`, `fresh_touch`, `_key`, `_arrow_at`, `_stood` |

**Modes** (`go(mode=...)`). `avoid` (no escort): looks cover the whole screen and every chain keeps clear of every
monster. `hunt` (with an escort, the default then): before each chain she shoots what's in reach, at most
`ON_WAY_TRIES` (5) times a platform, and what's in the way of a move along her platform (`MAX_FIGHTS`, 3 in a row).
`transit` (the hunt loop's trips to its objectives, and its stand-by trip at the end): only what's in the way,
without finishing what she hurt. With an
escort a chain keeps clear only of kinds whose touch counts (`Escort.threat`); on a map where none counts (the first
map) chains are planned blind.

**Monsters as the planner sees them.** A chain's monsters (`_chain_monsters`) are `MonsterTrack`s: every monster in the
look's state (the whole screen, 15 states a second), each walking the way perception says it heads at its kind's speed
from the game data (a standing one either way for up to `STAND_UNSURE_S`, 1 s), plus those her memory saw on the chain's
platforms within `TRIP_MEMORY_S` (2 s) that the look missed, the feed's tracks out of sight, and the monster the last cut
was for. `flow.danger` checks her body's box against each one's box wherever it can be by then, every 0.05 s of each leg.

**Her invulnerability.** After a touch she can't be touched for 1.45 s (`perception.touches.INVULNERABLE_S`). Chains are
planned with no touch counting before that ends, less `IMMUNE_MARGIN_S` (0.15 s), so she may pass a monster then
(`IMMUNE`); the planning's own time is taken out again before a chain goes (`IMMUNE_RECHECK`). No fight starts and the
trip's `until` isn't asked during that window (`POST_HIT`): fighting from wherever a hit knocked her kept her there.

**Feature flags.** Most behaviour since 2026-10-26 sits behind a module switch, each with its measurements: `TOUCH_CUTS`,
`IMMUNE`, `POST_HIT`, `REACT`, `REPLAN`, `KNOCK_REPLAN`, `LANDING_CLEAR`, `MEET_WALK`, `EVADE` with the contact rule
(`CONTACT`) and the evade review's R2-R7 (`WATCH_MOVES` R2, `STAND_WINDOW` R3, `AROUND_ALL` R4, `UNSEEN_AVOID` R5,
`QUEUE_CHECK` R6, `TOUCHER_S` R7), `ROPE_TOP`, `ROPE_CUT`, `ROPE_DROP`, `DROP_RELOOK`, `ROPE_HANG`
with `HANG_LONGER` and `HANG_TAKE`, `ARRIVE_STAND`, `PASS_WINDOW`. Measured and left off: `BLOCK_MEMORY`, `PASS_AVOID`,
`REFUGE_WORTH`, `TOUCHER_ALL`, `SAFE_PASS`, `QUEUE_SPREAD`.

**Like a player, not the same way every time.** Each trip weighs every move by a random 1 to 1 + `variety`
(`route.NOISE`, 0.35), kept through its replans, so near-equal routes take turns, and Flow varies where moves start.
Choosing among whole ways (`route.ROUTES` over 1, `--ways 3`) is off by default: 3 ways made as much EXP but picked up
fewer drops in the harness.

**Chain length.** `Flow.chain` stops a chain after 5 legs or once it passes 3.5 s (`flow.MAX_LEGS`, `MAX_SECONDS`): it
ends 'long', and the watch plans the next one late in it (`_look_ahead`, `_queue_next`) so she runs on.

**Small public helpers** others use: `leaves_at` (where the quickest way leaves her platform: the hunt loop),
`first_clear` (the first of several walk goals that is clear of a look's monsters: behavior.targeting),
`fresh_touch` and `rope_at_top` (behavior.hunter, behavior.fight).

key_items.name: Navigator
key_items.signature: class Navigator: def __init__(self, senses: Senses, actions: Actions, model: MapModel, *, log=print, health: Callable[[Scene], None] | None = None, escort: Escort | None = None, variety: float | None = None, rng: random.Random | None = None, memory=None, moves=None, danger: Callable[[], object] | None = None, price: Callable[[int, str], TopPrice | None] | None = None)
key_items.summary: Holds the route Planner, a Mover, a Flow (with her live key names: KeyNames), a monster Tracker and what persists between trips (when each move was last set off on, monsters already reacted to, the map's kinds whose touch counts). Each trip's random move weights live in its TripState.
key_items.details_md: Constructor hooks, all optional: `health(scene)` (the hunter's potions and safety stop), `escort` (behavior.fight.FightOnTheWay: fights on the way), `memory` (localization.memory: monsters seen anywhere), `moves` (behavior.keycheck.MoveWatch: told whether her jumps and runs moved her dot), `danger` (attack.danger model: breaks ties between refuge spots), `price(platform, kind)` (TopPrice: what her time up a rope is worth, for HANG_TAKE). `variety` defaults to route.NOISE (0.35); 0 for a retreat.

key_items.name: Navigator.go
key_items.signature: def go(self, dst: int, x: float | None = None, seconds: float = 180, max_misses: int = 6, until: Callable[[Scene], bool] | None = None, *, mode: str | None = None, scene: Scene | None = None, keep_off=(), vary: bool = True, stand_until: float | None = None, evade_s: float | None = None, refuge_s: float | None = None, toucher: bool = False, deadline_pass: bool = True, arrive_waits: int = 0) -> Trip
key_items.summary: A whole trip onto platform dst (and to x on it): begin, then step until it's over; while looks fail (LookLost) she stands still until the deadline.
key_items.details_md: `until(scene)` is asked before every chain: True ends the trip 'in position'. `scene` lets the caller's last look serve the first pass if no key went since and it shows her standing. `keep_off` platforms cost route.KEEP_OFF_S (8 s) a move onto them. The Lie Detector retreat passes its own budget (`evade_s`, `refuge_s`, `deadline_pass`, False while it lingers at a refuge, `toucher`, `arrive_waits`). Results: 'arrived', 'in position', 'timeout', 'too many misses', 'lost: not on any platform', 'no route from platform A to B'.

key_items.name: Navigator._pass
key_items.signature: def _pass(self, st: TripState) -> Trip | None
key_items.summary: One pass of a trip: the decision procedure from a look to a chain carried out.
key_items.details_md:
In order, each pass:
1. Ends the trip on its deadline (`timeout`, or `timeout (at a refuge)`) or after `max_misses` misses.
2. Unless this is a retreat's trip (`actions.kind` set), `client.check_alarm()`: the Lie Detector stops the trip.
3. Looks (`_look`: a fresh look kept from the last chain, else `Mover.locate(mobs=True, wide=not fight)`), calls
   `health(s)` (her potions and the safety stop, which raises), and ends 'in position' if `until(s)` says so (not
   while she's invulnerable after a touch).
4. `_onto_platform`: in the air, waits to land (`FALL_LOOKS` looks); on a rope, `Mover.off_rope`. Nowhere: 'lost'.
5. On the destination platform: shoots a monster between her and x (escort), checks the walk on (`_arrival_clear`),
   `Mover.walk_to(x)`, 'arrived'.
6. In hunt mode, shoots what's in reach here (`_shoot_on_the_way`) and looks again.
7. Plans (`_plan` -> `_route`), clears the way to the first move (escort), picks the monsters (`_chain_monsters`) and
   chains (`_chain` -> `Flow.chain`: legs, keys and why it ended: 'done', 'monster', 'long', 'unpredictable').
8. Meets a monster blocking the first move: `_meet` with an escort, else `_wait_for_monster`; either may end the pass
   (look again) or hand back a chain planned past it. With an escort and nothing to meet, `_clear_landing`
   (`LANDING_CLEAR`) may shoot or wait out a monster that makes the chain's last landing dear.
9. Drops the chain if planning ate into her invulnerability (`_immunity_spent`).
10. Carries out the chain (`_carry_out_chain`, replanned as it runs) or, with nothing chained, the first move alone
    (`_carry_out_move`: the Mover).
11. Checks for a rope's top (`_rope_top`), notes where she landed (`_note_landing`): a miss counts only if she ended
    elsewhere with no touch and no deliberate stop.

key_items.name: Navigator._route
key_items.signature: def _route(self, st: TripState, src: int, x: float, dst: int) -> tuple[list[Move] | None, tuple | None]
key_items.summary: The trip's route, weighed by its random weights and penalized (monster in the way, keep-off, can't); with route.ROUTES over 1 it chooses one of several ways and keeps it through replans.
key_items.details_md: Penalties (`_penalty`): `AVOID_SECONDS` (6 s) for a move a monster was in the way of within `AVOID_MEMORY_S` (4 s), route.KEEP_OFF_S for one onto a keep-off platform, `CANNOT_S` (60 s) for one the mover couldn't do. Choosing among ways happens only with `route.ROUTES` over 1 (default 1: the quickest by the weights) and a trip that varies (`vary`). A chosen way (`Choice`) is dropped once she has set off on its move, is past it, it costs more than the quickest by more than route.STRETCH of the quickest, or it would take her back onto a platform.

key_items.name: Navigator._chain_monsters
key_items.signature: def _chain_monsters(self, st: TripState, s: Scene, path: list[Move], start: float | None = None) -> tuple[list, list | None]
key_items.summary: The monsters a chain keeps clear of (and those its run-on tail must avoid): the whole state's, walking as perception has them head, plus remembered, hidden and last-cut ones.

key_items.name: Navigator._meet
key_items.signature: def _meet(self, st: TripState, s: Scene, path: list[Move], monsters: list, legs: list[Leg], why: str, planned_at: float, looked: float)
key_items.summary: With an escort: what to do about a monster whose touch counts blocking the route (shoot, way around, hop, wait, evade, last shot, pass regardless).
key_items.details_md:
With an escort, when a monster whose touch counts stopped the chain:
1. Her chains have stopped short of such monsters for `MEET_S` (8 s) without a move that got her where it was going:
   go regardless, blind (a backstop event).
2. The chain got some legs and stopped at a later one: shoot that monster from here if a star reaches it
   (`_shoot_ahead`), else carry out what chained.
3. The first move is blocked: shoot it from where she stands (`Escort.clear_for`), or from along her platform within
   `SHOOT_WALK` (150 units, `MEET_WALK`); at most `MAX_FIGHTS` (3) shots in a row.
4. A way around: the move, and each move of the next way offered that the same monsters block, cost `AVOID_SECONDS`
   (6 s) more for `AVOID_MEMORY_S` (4 s) (`_around`, `AROUND_TRIES` 8).
5. A hop over it (a chain with `hops=True`).
6. Wait `WAIT_S` (0.3 s), up to `WAIT_LOOKS` (6), only where she's safe standing (`_safe_to_stand`) and waiting can
   clear the way (`_worth_waiting`: its walk not known, it stands, or walking as seen it clears within `WAIT_AHEAD`,
   2.4 s).
7. Not safe here: the evade step (`_evade_step`).
8. A last look and shot at it (`LAST_SHOT`), then `_regardless`: the chain planned as if that monster weren't there,
   the others still kept clear of (a backstop event `NO_WAIT` or `WAIT_LOOKS`, with its episode).

key_items.name: Navigator._wait_for_monster
key_items.signature: def _wait_for_monster(self, st: TripState, s: Scene, path: list[Move], monsters: list, legs: list[Leg], why: str, planned_at: float, looked: float = 0.0) -> bool
key_items.summary: Without an escort, a monster blocking the first move: where she can stand safely and waiting can clear the way, first a way around, then up to WAIT_LOOKS waits; otherwise the evade step and, failing that, a pass (_go_past).

key_items.name: Navigator._evade_step
key_items.signature: def _evade_step(self, st: TripState, s: Scene, path: list[Move], monsters: list, looked: float) -> bool
key_items.summary: The contact rule, waiting at a refuge while it stays safe, or a new refuge, all within the blocked move's budget.
key_items.details_md: The contact rule (`CONTACT`): a monster seen live within `CONTACT_LIVE_S` (0.5 s) that touches her within `CONTACT_S` (0.25 s) whatever she does (standing, or running either way) is a touch taken as given: the chain is planned in the invulnerability window after it. A refuge (`_refuge`): the nearest spot along her platform within `EVADE_WALK` (150 units), at least `EVADE_STEP_MIN` (8) away and `EVADE_IN` (22) in from its ends, tried every `SPOT_STEP` (5), where the step and standing `EVADE_HOLD_S` (1.5 s) stay clear; else the quickest single move off her platform that chains clear and costs the trip at most `EVADE_MOVE_S` (1.5 s) more. Budget: `EVADE_S` (3.5 s) from the move's first block, `EVADE_REFUGES` (4), and not with `EVADE_DEADLINE_S` (4 s) or less left of the trip. Then `_go_past`: the chain planned without the blocking monster, one at a time, `PASS_TRIES` (3), else blind; with `PASS_WINDOW` left out only within the window its first touch would open.

key_items.name: Navigator._carry_out_move
key_items.signature: def _carry_out_move(self, st: TripState, s: Scene, path: list[Move], monsters=()) -> tuple[list[Move], Platform, Scene]
key_items.summary: The route's first move alone through the Mover, watched (cut on a touch, HP drop, off the move, a rope top to hang under) and its run-ups checked against the monsters.
key_items.details_md: MoveCut -> `recover` and replan (a touch starts the POST_HIT window). MoveRefused -> the move costs AVOID_SECONDS and counts a refusal (after `REFUSALS`, 3, it goes unchecked). ValueError (a move it can't do from here) -> `CANNOT_S` for the rest of the trip.

key_items.name: Navigator.follow
key_items.signature: def follow(self, legs, keys, hp: float, dst: int, why: str, trip: Trip, st: TripState | None = None, path: list[Move] | None = None, monsters=(), since: float | None = None, replan: bool = False) -> tuple[str, list]
key_items.summary: Sends a chain's plan and runs the watch; any exception (Ctrl+C included) cancels every plan it sent so no keys play on unwatched.
key_items.details_md: A chain cut off for length ('long') gets a tail (`_tail`): the plan keeps her running on with the arrow held (short of the next move by `RUN_ON_ROOM`, 50 units) or standing, long enough for a look to place her and the next chain to be planned. The plan goes out with `end_ms` = the predicted landing plus the tail, after `Actions.hold_back`, via `client.send` (name 'flow').

key_items.name: Navigator._watching
key_items.signature: def _watching(self, current, hp, dst, send, st, since, queued, sent, cut, stood, off_since, off_leg, ahead, over, first, moved, first_at, last_at, dot, glanced, top, checked, withdrawn) -> tuple[str, list]
key_items.summary: The glance loop while chains run: queue the next, check touches and the path, hang under a rope's top, react to monsters coming, replan, cut.
key_items.details_md:
Each turn of the loop waits for the feed's next frame, `GLANCE_S` (30 ms) at most, and takes the newest state
(perception gives 15 a second, each with the whole screen's monsters and their tracks):
- **Follow-on.** `LOOK_AHEAD` (0.9 s) before the chain's last landing, `_look_ahead` looks around; then a look placing her
  (`_check_at`: `CHECK_AFTER`, 0.05 s, after she's back on the ground for good, and no sooner than `CHECK_LEAD`, 0.25 s,
  before the plan ends), from which `_queue_next` plans and sends the next chain.
- **Its end.** With nothing to follow, a tail kept for a look is cut at the last leg's end; within `END_WATCH` (0.1 s) of
  the end it polls every 5 ms (`END_POLL_S`).
- **A glance** (`Senses.glance`: her minimap dot and HP), each with its frame's time.
- **Splices**: whether the player took the spliced plan (`client.taken`); if not, she stops.
- **Queue check** (`QUEUE_CHECK`): 2 glances before a queued chain whose first leg is a drop or a climb starts, its
  flight against the newest tracks; a meeting withdraws it.
- **Cuts**: a touch told since the look, or HP down by `HIT` (0.4%) -> 'touched'; standing `OFF_PATH_S` (0.109 s) off the
  planned path, or `OFF_LEG_S` (0.046 s) where the leg doesn't go, or still at a run's start while the plan has her
  `OFF_SPAN` (30 units) along -> 'off the path'; a landing the hunt wants to act on (`_landing_calls`); a climb whose way
  up is blocked -> hang (`ROPE_HANG`).
- **Monsters coming** (`REACT`): one the plan didn't know meets a leg ahead -> replan and splice (`_switch`), else stop
  where there's room. Every `BETTER_EVERY_S` (5 states) a replan for a better way.
- **On a cut**: cancel the running and queued plans, then hang, climb on after a touch on a rope (`_climb_on`), or wait
  for the knock's landing (`_knock_landing`).

key_items.name: Navigator._switch
key_items.signature: def _switch(self, st: TripState | None, running: _Running, dst: int, why: str, kind: str) -> _Running | None
key_items.summary: REPLAN: the running chain replanned from where she'll be when new keys can act, against the newest state, and handed over (spliced) if it's worth it and not too late.
key_items.details_md: Only from the ground, where the state has her on the plan's platform within `SPLICE_DRIFT` (20 units) of where the plan has her. 'monster': taken if anything chains. 'better': taken where the running chain stops short and the new one goes on past, or the new route is `SWITCH_GAIN_S` (0.25 s) cheaper; never within `SWITCH_MIN_S` (0.5 s) of the last switch, never the same way again. Dropped if the player would take it more than `SPLICE_LATE_S` (0.05 s) past its start or after a takeoff key (measured replans: p99 36 ms, the most 51).

key_items.name: Navigator._splice_point
key_items.signature: def _splice_point(self, running: _Running, t: float) -> tuple[float, Body] | None
key_items.summary: Where the running plan can be taken over at its time t at the soonest: on a run or a stand, there (with the arrow the plan holds then); in or about to start a flight or climb, where it ends.
key_items.details_md: A leg with a flight or a climb can't be changed from `KEY_COMMIT_S` (68 ms) before its takeoff key on (the key is the flight's start less `KEY_LEAD`: a jump's 65 ms lag, a drop's 0.28 s, a walk-off's stop time): the game has that key before new keys could act, so from then the splice point is where the leg lands her. With `SPLICE_PHYSICS` her place on a run comes from flow's own physics (`_ground`), not the span's straight line (off by up to 18 units early in a run).

key_items.name: Navigator._queue_next
key_items.signature: def _queue_next(self, st: TripState, running: _Running, ahead: _Ahead, dst: int, send) -> _Running | None
key_items.summary: Looks until she stands on the running chain's last platform, plans the next chain from there and sends it to start the moment the running plan ends.
key_items.details_md: Planned from a real look, not the predicted end: a landing 12.5 units off made the next running jump leave 12.5 units early, and landing late the next chain's keys came while she was still in the air. Refused (she stops) when she isn't seen standing in time (by `SEND_S`, 0.03 s, before the end), nothing chains, a monster is in the way of the next move (escort), or a monster seen could get near the chain.

key_items.name: Navigator._hang
key_items.signature: def _hang(self, rope: Rope, y: float, why: str) -> str
key_items.summary: ROPE_HANG: hang on the rope about 80 under its top until the way up clears, a touch is told, or the wait (HANG_S 2 s, longer for monsters predicted to walk off) is over; then climb the rest.
key_items.details_md: Judged at the start and every look (`_hang_judge`): `HANG_LONGER`: where every monster in the way is predicted to walk off, she hangs until that predicted clear plus `HANG_MARGIN_S` (0.3 s), if that is past `HANG_S` and at most `HANG_HORIZON_S` (3 s) from the hang's start; a monster that turns or stops puts it back to `HANG_S`; `HANG_TAKE` climbs at once where the rest of the wait, at what her time up there is worth (TopPrice.rate), costs more than the touch(es) and knock it avoids, and her HP stays over the safety reserve. Each hang is a 'rope_hang' telemetry event; a hang ending at HANG_S is a backstop event.

modules.concurrency: No threads of its own: it runs on the calling hunt's thread. While a chain plays it waits for each new perception state (up to GLANCE_S, 30 ms; states come 15 a second from the perception feed, a separate process) and glances at it, while the elevated player process plays the plans at the same time. A glance with no state for GLANCE_LOST_S raises LookLost (Senses.glance).

gotchas: Chains are planned from a look that shows her standing, never from where the last chain was predicted to end.
Her minimap dot can sit still for 63 ms in mid-air (near a jump's top, or within a minimap pixel at full speed): standing is judged over STILL_S and never while the plan has her airborne.

Hanging on a rope just under a platform's top, her dot snaps onto the platform (from up to 33 units under it; 17 by a rope since localization.pose.ROPE_TOP_GAP): a chain whose dot never moved there means she's on the rope, where a jump or an arrow does nothing (ROPE_TOP, Mover.off_rope).
A replan is only spliced in from the ground: in a flight or past a takeoff key the next state asks again.
With a player started before splices existed, a replan cuts the running plan and resends: every key is let go for 15-35 ms.
The Lie Detector check at each pass and hang glance raises LieDetectorAlarm, except on a retreat's own trip (actions.kind set).
TripState.paused shifts the trip's clocks after a LookLost stand-still, and drops looks and sightings from before it.
Most of its behaviour is switched by module-level flags; tests and the harness flip them to measure each.

modules.title: Mover
modules.tagline: One route move at a time, closed loop: look, one key plan, settle, look.
modules.summary: Carries out a single route move (motion.route.Move) from wherever she stands, the way a player does it: run toward the end and jump on the way, run at a rope and jump onto it holding up, walk and drop in one go. The navigator hands it the moves a chain can't predict; the hunter uses it to get her off ropes. Its key plans go through Actions (locks respected), or, when the navigator watches the move, out with client.send and a check between glances.
modules.details_md:
**Looking.** `locate()` asks `Senses.look` until a look places her (`where` set): up to 40 tries 0.25 s apart (about
10 s), moving the mouse inside the game on the 4th (a tooltip from another program once hid the minimap), then
`RuntimeError("can't find her minimap dot")`. Its first look waits for her keys' effect to show
(`Senses.fresh_after`). `settle(seconds=2)` looks every 0.08 s until two looks in a row have her on the same platform with
her dot within 0.6 minimap px: she has stopped. With `since` (her dot where the move began) it also sets `still`, whether
every look had her dot there: keys that moved her nowhere, which the navigator reads as "on a rope under its top".

**`do(move, s)`** dispatches on `move.kind`, then returns `settle()`:
- `jump` (`_run_and_jump`): run toward the end and press jump so she leaves the ground at the move's takeoff (or
  `route.JUMP_FROM`, 33 units, from the end). A run shorter than `MIN_RUN` (15 units: keyed 155 ms after the arrow, past
  the 150 ms blind spot, so she leaves at full speed) first walks back to the move's start. The arrow is let go just
  before she lands (`flow.ARROW_LAG`), the flight time from `physics.fly`.
- `walk_off`: from at least `MIN_RUN` in from the end (else she backs off to `MIN_RUN + RUN_UP_SPARE` first), so she
  leaves at full speed; held long enough for where she lands plus 20 units.
- `drop`: walk to within 20 units of the spot, then down, jump 120 ms later, down let go at 200 ms
  (`DROP_DOWN_UP_MS`). Where a drop there wouldn't go through (by a rope's top, a foothold that forbids it) or would come
  down by a cliff (`route.drop_clear`), it walks to the nearest spot that would (`route.drop_spots`), or exactly to the
  move's own spot (`DROP_AT_SPOT`).
- `climb` (`_climb`): run at the rope and jump `grab_lead` (WALK_SPEED x JUMP_SPEED / GRAVITY, about 41 units) before it,
  up held from the jump on; walk in holding up where the rope comes down to within 10 of her feet; jump straight up
  from under it (within 6 units). Up is held `climb_ms(height)`: height / CLIMB_SPEED + 500 ms. A rope ending more than
  87 above her feet (ROPE_REACH 95 less GRAB_MARGIN 8) raises ValueError. Near a portal, up goes down only 100 ms after
  the jump key (`PORTAL_UP_MS`).
- `climb_down`: line up on the rope's top (walk within 12 units, then up to 3 on-screen nudges to within 6 px of the rope
  found within 70 px of where the map puts it), then hold down.
- `jump_up`: walk to the takeoff and jump straight up.
- `rope_jump` (`_rope_jump`): onto the rope, a look, a climb to the move's hang height if off by more than 15 units,
  then the arrow and the jump 40 ms later, up held for a rope it jumps onto or the arrow let go just before landing. Not
  on the rope at the look: nothing more, the navigator replans.

**Watched moves.** With `watch` set (the navigator's `_move_watch`), `_send` sends the plan with `client.send` and asks
`watch()` between glances; a reason (a touch, HP dropping, off the move, a rope top to hang under) cancels the plan,
every key let go, and raises `MoveCut`. With `clear(x0, x1)` set, a run-up's or back-off's walk is checked against the
monsters first: into one raises `MoveRefused` before any key goes (a climb's back-off switches to climbing from under the
rope if that walk is clear).

**Ropes outside a trip.** `off_rope` gets her off a rope: up (held 0.9 s) if she's within 70 of a top that leads onto
a platform; down past its bottom onto the platform under it where the top leads onto none (959's, under 17's block) or
the caller asks for `down` (up did nothing); else a sideways jump toward the side whose fall lands on a platform.
`hang` / `unhang` put her on a rope at a height and back (attack.ropes' places to wait).

modules.title: Actions
modules.tagline: Her actions as key plans: throws, jump throws, jump backs, walks, pick-ups, potions.
modules.summary: Turns one action of hers at a time into a key plan and blocks until the player has played it. It never decides anything (attack and behavior do). It keeps the timing every plan must respect (her 730 ms attack lock, the 0.8 s arrow lock after an attack key) and which way she faces, by her keys and by the frame, which decides whether a throw taps the arrow to turn her first.
modules.details_md:
**Plans.** `tap(t, key)` is a press at t ms and a release `TAP_MS` (40 ms) later. `play(events, name)` holds the plan
back (`hold_back`), asks `before_play` (the hunter's stop check: `gamelab stop` since the look), then
`client.submit(events, lead_ms=0, focus=True)` and waits for the result; `ended()` then records when her last key went,
so the next look waits for its effect.

**Locks.** In the game a regular attack ignores jump and attack keys for 730 ms (`COMBAT.attack_lock_ms`), and an arrow
pressed within about 0.62 s of an attack key moves her only from about 0.79 s after it. `hold_back(events)` sleeps just
long enough that no jump or attack key in the plan comes before `lock_until`, and no arrow before `arrow_until`
(`ARROW_LOCK_MS` = 800 ms after the attack key). Every plan that can press them goes through it: Actions' own, the
mover's and the navigator's chains. A throw sets `lock_until` to 730 + 60 ms from the plan's end
(`THROW_LOCK_EXTRA_MS`), a jump throw or jump back 730 + 160 (`JUMP_THROW_LOCK_EXTRA_MS`).

**Throws.**
- `throw(direction)`: wait out the lock (or `lock_watch`, which can call the attack off frame by frame), ask
  `still(direction)` (a kill shown since the decision drops it), tap the arrow unless `faces(direction)`, then tap the
  attack key `_attack_key` picks: the regular attack, Lucky Seven or Magic Claw with `skill`, or what `choose` says
  (behavior.attacks).
- `jump_throw(direction, key_ms, way)`: in the air the attack throws a star even point-blank, where on the ground the
  claw only swipes (9-11 damage against 30-70). The attack key comes `key_ms` after the jump key (40 ms by default).
  Turning, she taps the arrow in the air 60 ms after the jump key and attacks 120 ms after it at the soonest; with
  `air_turn=False` the tap goes first and the jump waits until 205 ms into the plan (`physics.JUMP_THROW_TURN_MS`)
  for the tap's walk to stop. `way` ±1 jumps forward (the arrow
  held, the jump 40 ms on, the arrow let go 100 ms after the jump key). The magician (`ground_only`) throws from the
  ground instead.
- `jump_back(direction)`: at a monster too close, run away `JB_RUN_MS` (150 ms, past the kick's blind spot), jump, tap
  toward it in mid-air at 210 ms and attack at 270 ms, so the star (about 520 ms after the key) leaves as she lands
  about 90 units away. Never dropped.

**Facing.** Her keys (`facing`: the way her last plan's arrow or throw turned her; None after any move) and the frame
(`see`, given perception.heading's reading after every look). `heading` is the frame's when it's newer than her last
arrow, else her keys'. A frame isn't believed within `HEADING_SETTLE_S` (0.2 s) of her last arrow, while a navigator
chain plays (its arrows aren't known here: `sent_at` blinds it until the navigator sets `facing`), or during her attack
unless it's strong. `faces` lets a throw skip the turn tap only by her keys or a strong frame: a weak frame can add a tap
but never take one away (every frame read the wrong way on 2026-10-24 was weak, and a star the wrong way costs more
than a tap). A hit with no frame telling makes her heading unknown, so the next throw taps. `retap()` forces a tap after
her throws stop landing. `keys_say(t)` tells perception.heading which way her keys say beyond doubt she faces in a
frame (her last arrow `LEARN_AFTER_S`, 0.25 s, or more before it, no hit, no chain playing), so it can learn her
pictures; `ended()` records when her last key went (the looks wait for its effect), on the `moves_only` copy's parent too.

**The rest.** `walk(direction, units)` holds the arrow `hold_ms(units)` with pick-up tapped every 150 ms and 200 ms
past the release; `pick_here()` presses pick-up 4 times 120 ms apart (one item a press; a pig drops several);
`drink()`, `feed_pet()` (kind `pet_food`, allowed with the alarm up), `nudge_mouse()` (the pointer moved inside the
game, never a click: a tooltip once hid the minimap). `moves_only()` makes her Lie Detector retreat's copy: arrows, jump,
up and down only, every plan of kind `retreat`, the locks shared, her last key told to both.

modules.title: Client
modules.tagline: Mails key plans to the elevated player through lab/inbox; reads answers in lab/outbox.
modules.summary: The only way the unelevated stack gets keys into the game. `send` writes a plan as JSON into lab/inbox/<id>.json; the player claims it (renames it .running), plays it and writes lab/outbox/<id>.json; `wait` polls for that file every 10 ms. It also cuts plans short or withdraws them (`cancel`), hands over a replacement mid-play (`splice`), and sends nothing but four allowed plan kinds while the Lie Detector alarm is up.
modules.details_md:
**The mailbox.** Everything is a file in `gamelab/lab/` (`paths.INBOX`, `paths.OUTBOX`), written atomically: a `.tmp`
beside the target, then `replace`.

| File | Written by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `inbox/<id>.json` | `send` | a plan waiting for the player |
| `inbox/<id>.running` | the player | claimed (renamed): it can't be withdrawn now, only cut short |
| `inbox/<id>.cancel` | `cancel`, `cut_running` | stop pressing now and let go of every key |
| `inbox/<running id>.splice` | `splice` | a plan to take over from the running one at its `at_ms` |
| `outbox/<id>.json` | the player | the result: `sent` (each key as pressed, ms into the plan), `problems`, `error`, `trail` |
| `outbox/<id>.npz` | the player | recorded frames and their times, if the plan asked for capture |

A plan id is `HHMMSS_<name>_<4 hex>` (64 characters at most), its name cut to letters, digits, `-` and `_`, because the
player keeps only those of the file name: a plan named "pet food" was answered as "petfood" and its result never found.

**send, wait, submit.** `send` writes `{events, capture: {fps, duration_ms, scale, lead_ms[, crop]}, focus[, end_ms,
window_client, kind]}` and returns the id at once. `end_ms` makes the plan last that long even past its last key: the
navigator queues its next chain this way, to start the moment the running one ends. `wait(id, timeout=120)` polls every
`POLL_S` (10 ms); reads the result with up to 50 tries 20 ms apart (Windows can still hold a file just moved into place:
a sweep once crashed on PermissionError); deletes it and any cancel file left over; loads frames from the `.npz`; and
raises `PlayerError` on an `error` (`LieDetectorAlarm` when it's the Lie Detector's). On timeout it deletes the
unclaimed plan and says how to start the player (`python -m gamelab player --elevate`). `submit` is `send` then `wait`.

**Cutting short.** `cancel(id)`: a plan still `.json` is deleted (withdrawn: True, no result will come); a `.running`
one gets a `.cancel` file and the player lets go of everything (False: wait for its result). A plan already over gets no
cancel file, since one made then was never read and stayed in the inbox. `cut_running()` (from `gamelab stop`) touches a
cancel for every plan in the inbox, whoever sent it. Cancelling a splice the player hasn't taken yet withdraws the
`.splice` file and cuts the plan it was meant to take over from. `busy()` says whether any plan is waiting or playing.
Small helpers for other modules: `player_up()` (a player's pid in `lab/player.json` is alive), `started(pid)` (a
process's creation time, so a reused pid isn't taken for the same process), `alarm_up()` and `alarm_age()`.

**Splices** (the navigator's replans, from 2026-10-30). `splice(running_id, events, at_ms, held, end_ms)` writes
`<running_id>.splice`, not a `.json`, so the player never takes it as a plan of its own; a later splice into the same
plan replaces one not taken yet. At `at_ms` on the running plan's clock the player drops the old plan's remaining keys,
lets go of held keys not in `held`, presses those in `held` not held, and plays the new events; the old plan's result
gets the problem `spliced`. `taken(id)` answers True, False (the old plan ended first: the splice is withdrawn) or None
(not known yet). `can_splice()` reads `lab/player.json`, which the player writes as it starts (`splice: 1`, its pid), and
checks the pid is alive with `OpenProcess` and `GetExitCodeProcess` (never Windows' `os.kill`, which ends a process). A
player started before splices existed writes none, and the navigator cuts and resends instead.

**The Lie Detector.** `send` and `splice` call `check_alarm()` (raises while `lab/ALARM.json` exists) unless the plan
has a `kind` from `alarm.PLAN_KINDS`: `pet_food`, `retreat`, `lie_cursor`, `lie_ok`, which the player takes or refuses
by its own rules. `wait` withdraws a waiting plan without a kind as soon as the alarm appears. `move_lie_cursor`,
`click_lie_answer` and `click_lie_ok` build the mouse-only plans for the mini-game, Violetta's quiz and the pass's OK
button (a move, the left button down at 1,000 ms and up 80 ms later), withdrawing them if the round ends first. Retreat
plans never bring the game to the front (`focus` False).

modules.title: Keymap
modules.tagline: Her keys followed to where the game's Key Bindings window puts them, and remembered.
modules.summary: When the game's KEY BINDINGS window is read (behavior.keycheck, `gamelab keys --read`), `follow` moves each of her keys to wherever the window shows its function, or turns it off, and says when the hunt must stop. The result is remembered per character and becomes the next command's starting keys (`at_start`), and her moves' and pet food's keys are published for the elevated player's Lie Detector allowance.
modules.details_md:
**Why.** On 2026-10-28 the user, asked whether keys moved in the game should stop the hunt or be followed, answered
"Follow them", and whether the binding read should be kept, "Remember it". Until then the hunt pressed `config.toml`'s
`[keys]` whatever the game had.

**`follow(keys, fn, illegible)`.** `fn` is the window reader's map (`perception.keybindings.Reader.functions`): key ->
the function drawn on it, a picture's name, or None. For each bound field of her `GameKeys` it looks up the function
the window should show (`FUNCTION_OF`: attack -> ATTACK, jump -> JUMP, the arrows -> MOVE LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN, pick_up
-> PICK UP, sit -> SIT, plus the pictures the reader knows: Lucky Seven, pet food, her chair, the magician's skills),
and then:

- the function is on her key still: kept;
- it's on another key she may press: moved there (`moved`);
- the window can't tell (her key's cell illegible, not drawn, or a picture the reader doesn't know): kept, in `unknown`;
- it's on no key she may press: `off`. Keys never followed onto are `NEVER` (Esc, the backslash that opens the window,
  F1-F4, F12) plus config.toml's `[hotkeys]` and `[control]` keys (`never()`); her moves and pet food also avoid the alarm's unsafe keys (`ALARM_UNSAFE`).
  A field in `NEEDED` (her five moves, Lucky Seven, pet food, Magic Claw) sets `stop`: the hunt can't go on without it.
  Her regular attack stays bound (behavior.keycheck turns it off for the run); other fields become None.

The game binds one function per key, so a key kept as "unknown" that another of her functions moved onto is turned off
too, and said.

**Remembered** (`lab/keybindings-<character>.json`). `remember` writes the keys with when and off which saved frame
they were read, the preset, the whole function map, config.toml's keys then and whether the game had Attack on no key;
written whole (a `.tmp`, then `os.replace`). `at_start(config_keys)` reads it back and returns a `Start`: no file ->
config.toml's keys; unreadable, or failing `problem` (unknown fields, a name config.toml can't name, arrows, jump or
attack unbound, two functions on one key, a NEVER key, or alarm keys the allowance can't take) -> config.toml's, with the
reason in `source`. A file marked by `suspect` (a doubt about a key that the run couldn't check:
behavior.hunter.Hunter.keys_doubted) is also left out until a new read writes it: the review of 2026-10-28 found a
stale MOVE RIGHT on E coming back at every start. A remembered "Attack on no key" is said but not kept: the regular
attack is tried again (5 presses without effect doubt it). `forget` deletes the file (`gamelab keys --forget`).

**Published** (`lab/alarm_keys.json`). With the Lie Detector alarm up the only key plans the player lets through are her
retreat's moves and her pet food (besides the mouse-only Lie Detector plans), and it must know which keys those are. `publish(keys)` writes the `ALARM_FIELDS` (left, right, jump, up, down,

started again (which costs the user a UAC click).

modules.title: Timeline
modules.tagline: MapleHelper's combo code run on a virtual clock; her keys and timing loaded.
modules.summary: Turns MapleHelper's own combos and actions into exact key timelines by running them against a fake engine context whose `wait` only advances a clock, so tests and the `combo` and `do` commands play exactly what the helper plays. It also loads her setup: `config.toml` with her keys as last read off the game (`keymap.at_start`), and the simulator's fixed key sets.
modules.details_md:
**The virtual clock.** maplehelper's combo scripts are written against an engine context, `maplehelper.engine.Ctx`,
which presses keys through a `send(key, down)` callback and sleeps with `wait(ms)`. `_Clock` subclasses `Ctx`: its
send (`_record`) appends `[round(now), key.name, "down" | "up"]` to a list, and its `wait` adds the milliseconds to
`now` instead of sleeping. Display output goes to maplehelper's `_Silent`, `slow=False`. Running a combo's
`script(clock)` therefore yields, with no real time passing, the exact key timeline the live helper would send.

- `combo_events(name, facing, start_ms, keys, timing)` runs one combo of `maplehelper.combos.COMBOS` from `start_ms`.
  It first records both arrows released (the helper's runner starts clean), ends with `release_all()`, and returns the
  events and the end time.
- `action_events(fn, args, facing, keys, timing)` does the same for one `maplehelper.actions` move from 0 (the
  `gamelab do` command).
- `chain(name, facing, count, keys, timing)` plays `count` copies back to back, the way the helper runs a queued press,
  and returns each copy's start too (`gamelab combo --chain`).

**Her setup.** `her_setup(regular_attack=False, remembered=True)` loads `config.toml` (`paths.CONFIG`). Where the
character this process plays (`gamelab.character.active()`) isn't the thief and has keys in her profile, those replace
`[keys]` (the magician's Magic Claw on her own key). With `remembered`, the keys returned are those last read off the
game's KEY BINDINGS window (`keymap.at_start`), else `config.toml`'s; `cfg.keys` stays `config.toml`'s either way.
`regular_attack=True` clears Lucky Seven and Magic Claw so throws use the plain attack key (no MP). It returns
`(config, keys, timing)`; gamelab's commands (`gamelab/__main__.py`) take their setup from it.

**The simulator's keys.** `SIM_KEYS` (her bindings up to 2026-10-22: attack f, Lucky Seven g, potions r and t, no pet),
`SIM_KEYS_PET` (from 2026-10-23, West Rocky Mountain II: attack ctrl, Lucky Seven shift, no potion keys because her pet
drinks them, pet food u) and `SIM_KEYS_MAGE` (from 2026-11-02: the magician's Magic Claw on shift, no Lucky Seven) are
fixed on purpose: the golden traces name keys, and a change to her live bindings must not change what the simulator
records. In the simulator they are names only: it acts on what each is bound to.

flows.title: One pass of a trip
flows.summary: How the navigator gets from a look to keys: plan the route, pick the monsters, chain the moves, deal with what blocks them, carry the chain out, then look again.
flows.trigger: behavior calls Navigator.go (the tour, the retreat) or begin then step (the hunt loop) with a platform to reach

steps.text: begin makes a TripState (180 s by default, a mode from the escort); step runs one pass at a time until it's over. A LookLost has her stand still until looks work again, the trip's clocks paused.
Deadline, misses and the Lie Detector alarm checked; a look with the monsters (or the one the last chain left); her potions and the safety stop; `until` may end the trip 'in position'.
The look: Senses.look until it places her; in the air or on a rope, the navigator waits for her to land or gets her off first.
The route from motion.route.Planner, each move weighed by the trip's random weights, with extra cost for moves a monster blocked, keep-off platforms and moves the mover couldn't do.
The monsters the chain keeps clear of: the whole state's, walking as perception has them head at their kind's speed, plus those her memory and the feed know but the look missed.
As many moves as can be predicted, chained into one key timeline from where she stands, stopping short of a leg a monster could touch her on.

A monster blocking the first move: with an escort shoot it, go around, hop, wait, evade, or pass it regardless (and, nothing to meet, _clear_landing for a monster by the last landing); without, _wait_for_monster then the evade step.
The chain goes out and is watched (follow); with nothing chained, the first move alone goes to the Mover, watched.
Where she ended against where the chain should have: elsewhere with no touch and no deliberate stop is a miss. The next pass plans from where she is.

flows.title: A chain running: glances, cut-offs and the next chain queued
flows.summary: While a chain's plan plays, the navigator glances at her about 15 times a second, cuts the plan on a touch or when she's off its path, and plans the next chain late in this one so she runs on without stopping.

steps.text: The chain waits just long enough that no jump or attack key falls in her attack lock and no arrow in the arrow lock.
The plan goes into lab/inbox with end_ms (its predicted landing plus any tail), not waited for.
The elevated player claims the plan (renames it .running), brings the game to the front if the plan asks (`focus`), refuses it if the game still isn't in front, and presses its keys on time.
Each glance: a touch told since the look or HP down by 0.4% cuts it; off the planned path for 0.109 s cuts it; a monster coming into a leg ahead has it replanned.
0.9 s before the last landing a look around: with an escort, a reason to stop where it ends (the trip's until, a target in reach) means no follow-on.
Once she's back on the ground, a look places her standing on the platform; the next chain is planned from there (about 5 ms) and sent to start the moment this plan ends.
On a cut, the running and queued plans are cancelled: the player stops and lets go of every key.
After a cut, a look once she has stopped (or, after a touch, the first state with her landed); after a clean end, the look the next pass will use.

flows.title: Replanning mid-chain with a splice
flows.summary: A monster the plan didn't know comes into a leg still to come: the chain is replanned from where she'll be 40 ms on and handed to the player to take over from the running plan, the arrow held kept held.
flows.trigger: a glance's state shows a monster meeting a leg ahead (REACT), or BETTER_EVERY_S has passed

steps.text: The newest state's monster tracks the plan didn't know, checked with flow.danger against the legs from REACT_LEAD_S (0.25 s) on.
Where the running plan can be taken over SPLICE_LEAD_S (40 ms) from now: on the ground there; in or about to start a flight, not yet.
Only where the state has her within 20 units of where the plan does; replanned against the whole state, the arrow held carried into the new chain; dropped if done too late.
Spliced if the player takes splices, else the running plan is cut and the new one sent at once.
Writes lab/inbox/<running id>.splice with the new events, at_ms and the keys to keep held.
At at_ms of the running plan's clock the player drops its remaining keys, keeps the held arrow down and plays the new events; the old plan's result says 'spliced'.
The watch learns the splice was taken (or not: the old plan ended first, and she stops).

flows.title: A throw, from decision to the game
flows.summary: How one action becomes keys: locks waited out, a turn tap only if needed, the attack key chosen, the plan mailed to the player and waited for, then the locks set for the next one.
flows.trigger: attack.stance / behavior.fight decides a throw at a monster

steps.text: Waits out her attack lock (or behavior.targeting's frame-by-frame watch), then asks `still`: a kill shown since the decision drops the throw.
A turn tap (50 ms, then 30 ms to settle) only if she doesn't surely face the target by her keys or a strong frame.
The regular attack, her skill (Lucky Seven, Magic Claw), or what the attack choice says; none: no throw.
